column1: # scripts/verify/mutants.tsv - the mutant catalogue
# One row per mutant: the source change that reintroduces the defect a test
# claims to cover. `tests.tsv` selects a mutant by name (`red = mutant:<name>`);
# this file says what that name does. Nothing here is executed: the engine is
# riscv_mutant_apply() in common.cmake, and it treats the file as text -- it
# knows nothing about SystemVerilog.
#   name <TAB> file <TAB> find <TAB> replace <TAB> why
# name      the string tests.tsv names as `mutant:<name>`
# file      path relative to the repository root
# find      the exact text to replace; it must occur EXACTLY once in file,
#           otherwise the mutant is stale and the gate aborts
# replace   the text that reintroduces the defect
# why       one line, printed when the mutant is applied and by --list
# '#' starts a comment line; a comment block above a row is that mutant's
# rationale. `;` is escaped by riscv_tsv_rows()/riscv_tsv_cell(), so SV
# statements with a semicolon are fine in a cell. The root-cause narrative
# stays in doc/verification.md (G-20/G-26/G-27, FR-12); this file only says
# what the mutation does.
# T-06 (FR-12): the pre-fix core ignored the address low bits and always
# extended the byte at the highest address, so 8 of the 12 T-06 cases stored
# the wrong value. Pinning the lane to 3 reproduces exactly that.

column4: assign ld_lane = 2'b11; // negative control: lane never selected
column5: the sub-word lane is not selected from the address (pre-fix FR-12)

column1: # T-08 (NFR-05): rv32ui-p-simple has no test case; the verdict rests on ADDI
# producing 1 and the store reaching tohost. Ignoring the second operand turns
# `li gp,1` into `li gp,0` and breaks `la t5,tohost`, so the harness must
# report SANITY: TIMEOUT plus a UVM error.
sanity-addi
column4: alu_result = alu_data1.s_data; // negative control: ADD ignores the second operand
column5: ADDI/ADD ignore their second operand, so `li gp,1` writes 0 and the pass store writes 0

column1: # T-09 (WP-4b): T-09 sets is_active=UVM_PASSIVE and requires the monitor only.
# Removing the guard builds the driver/sequencer in passive mode.
passive-agent-always-active
column4: if (1'b1) begin // negative control: UVM_PASSIVE ignored
column5: the agent builds the driver/sequencer even when is_active=UVM_PASSIVE

column1: # T-10 (G-27): reverting pc_id to the current `pc` misaligns the decoder PC by
# one instruction: a branch at 0xa0 targets 0x53c instead of 0x538.
branch-redirect
column4: pc_id <= pc; // negative control: one-instruction PC misalignment
column5: the decoder sees the next instruction's PC, so a branch target is +4 (G-27)

column1: # T-11 (G-26): alu_ex is the EX source of the ALU/jump forwarding; leaving it
# unknown loses the predecessor's value.
forward-rs1
column4: assign alu_ex = 'x; // negative control: EX forward source missing
column5: the EX-stage forward source is unknown, so the predecessor's value is lost (G-26)

column1: # T-12 (G-20): slicing imm[20:0] zero-extends a negative offset and sends the
# branch to the 0x200000-family; rv32ui-p-beq times out.
negative-branch
column4: jump_addr = base_addr + imm[20:0]; // negative control: zero-extended offset
column5: a negative branch/jump offset is zero-extended (G-20)

column1: # T-13 (FR-11 / G-08): rv32ui-p-sb walks every byte lane. Dropping the lane
# shift leaves the stored byte at lane 0 while the strobe selects the addressed
# byte, so every SB above lane 0 writes a zero.
store-lane-offset
column4: rs2_lane.u_data = rs2_pipeline.u_data; // negative control: byte store ignores the lane
column5: the byte value is not placed in the addressed lane (G-08)

column1: # T-14 (FR-11 / G-22): rv32ui-p-sh stores at offsets 0 and 2. A halfword
# strobe of 4'b1111 contradicts the halfword width and claims two bytes the
# store did not drive.
store-strb-all
column4: data_wr_strb_ex = 4'b1111; // negative control: halfword strobe drives all four bytes
column5: a halfword store announces four bytes (G-22)

column1: # T-15 (FR-11 / G-08, G-22): rv32ui-p-st_ld mixes byte, half and word. Forcing
# the width port to byte makes every halfword/word store report 2'b00 next to a
# 2- or 4-bit strobe, which the strb_checker rejects even when the image's own
# software verdict would pass.
store-width-cast
column4: assign data_rd_wr_ctrl = 2'b00; // negative control: width port forced to byte
column5: the width port reports byte for every access (FR-11, the old one-bit cast)
